lens: TECHNICAL: completeness, build result, and how far the renderer can be extended for HD. Re-inspected the existing clone at scratchpad/repos/ra2-games__ra2 (HEAD f25986b; after git fetch, origin/main is unchanged), re-ran the build and the unit tests, and grepped for the claimed features and hooks.

refuted_claims.claim: The host receives only finished frames and cannot see objects, tiles, depth or water. The only way to get more is a very large reverse-engineering effort that hooks gamemd.exe draw routines.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The host already has two data paths beyond VmFrame that need no guest trampolines. (1) The DirectDraw shim owns every guest surface. src/vm86/shim/stateGraphics.ts:48-58 exposes inspectSurfaceObjects() and inspectSurface(object), which return width, height, pitch, bpp and pixels for each surface. The real-game test harness already uses them (tests/real-game/helpers/runVmSmoke.ts:625,1923,1939). So separating intermediate or offscreen surfaces, or the sidebar and tactical layers, is host-side plumbing and not guest reverse engineering. (2) The host reads guest memory directly at known addresses. src/games/yr/performance.ts reads the YR frame counter at 0xA8ED84 and game speed at 0xA8EB60. src/games/yr/commandQueue.ts reads EventClass rings at 0xA802C8 and 0x8B41F8. docs/GAME_PERFORMANCE.md:79 says these layouts come from YRpp's EventClass.h and QueueClass.h and were checked against both executables.
refuted_claims.correction: The host does not see depth or object draw calls today (that part is VERIFIED). But it already has host-readable access to all DirectDraw surfaces and to raw guest memory. The pinned YR build lines up with at least some YRpp addresses: VERIFIED for the frame-counter global, and the EventClass/QueueClass layouts according to the repo's doc. So a read-only state bridge (object lists, positions, facing, water and shroud masks) can build on the open-source YRpp address map instead of fresh reverse engineering. That is still hard, but for YR it is a months-scale prototype, not years (INFERENCE). RA2 1.006 has no comparable public map, so it remains much harder.

refuted_claims.claim: Option (3) needs YRpp-level reverse engineering of the exact gamemd.exe and game.exe builds, done separately for RA2 and YR, and amounts to many months to years.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: For YR, the YRpp-level reverse engineering already exists publicly, and the repo already consumes it against the pinned gamemd.exe 1.001 hash (docs/GAME_PERFORMANCE.md:79,93; src/games/yr/*.ts address tables). docs/RESHADE_ADAPTATION.md also records that a Windows precedent (the Toumao ReShade plugin) already exports ZBUFFER, WATER, SHROUD, LIGHT and TOPMASK textures and replaces animations and voxel meshes on real YR. So the hook targets are known and not speculative.
refuted_claims.correction: Treat option (3) as YR-first and bounded, not open-ended. A realistic first milestone: export Z-buffer, water and shroud masks via guest hooks (or surface reads), plus one unit with HD-sprite replacement. The docs themselves propose exactly this step. RA2-only support would need separate reverse engineering. None of this is implemented yet; only LaserBlit passthrough exists (VERIFIED).

refuted_claims.claim: The engine is capped at 1920x1080 (listed as a risk and under feature completeness).
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The cap is only a UI whitelist array in src/games/resolution.ts (GAME_RESOLUTIONS, 7 entries). The patch writes arbitrary ScreenWidth and ScreenHeight into RA2.INI/RA2MD.INI [Video]. Nothing in the code shows the 1920x1080 limit is an engine limit. The real cost of a higher resolution is emulation throughput, because the guest software renderer scales with pixel count. That cost is unmeasured.
refuted_claims.correction: The 1920x1080 cap is a project policy and can be lifted with a small code change; this does not change the evaluation's main point. The underlying limit the evaluation states correctly still holds: at a higher resolution you see more of the map, not sharper art, and CPU emulation cost grows.

refuted_claims.why_wrong: docs/RA2_NETWORK_RELIABILITY.md:100 documents an RA2_BROWSER_PLAYERS=8 browser harness. It verifies 8 native slots, sends a deploy command per player and checks consistent state across all VMs. The doc also says real 8-player acceptance needs more memory or distributed hosts.
refuted_claims.correction: The 2-player weak-network short match is the validated path. An 8-player deploy-consistency harness exists, but the repo does not show it has been accepted on real hardware. Long or 8-player matches remain unvalidated.

refuted_claims.claim: Adding bridge hooks 'fights the project's own rule against game-specific code in vm86'.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: docs/RESHADE_ADAPTATION.md says game-specific hooks belong in game modules (src/games/ra2, src/games/yr) and not in generic vm86. That is a code-placement rule, and the doc itself prescribes how to follow it. It is not an obstacle.
refuted_claims.correction: The layering rule tells you where the bridge code goes (src/games/yr/* plus a generic hypercall or VmFrame extension). It does not block the work.

confirmed_claims: Build is VERIFIED again: `pnpm run build` exited 0 in about 8.5 s wall time (log: scratchpad/repos/ra2vm_verify_build.log). dist/ is 6.1 MB, with v86 wasm 2,101.62 kB, 7zz wasm 1,651.93 kB, vmWorker 742.72 kB and page 871.32 kB. The only warning was chunk size over 500 kB.
Unit tests are VERIFIED again: 128 files and 918 tests all passed in 4.63 s (scratchpad/repos/ra2vm_verify_test.log).
Installed versions: v86 0.5.441+g847e34d, TypeScript 5.9.3, Vite 6.4.3, React 19.3.0, onnxruntime-web 1.29.0. About 38,094 lines of TS/TSX in src/.

There is no Three.js. A whole-word grep for 'three' only finds English prose in comments, and node_modules has no three package. The renderer is raw WebGL2 GLSL ES 3.0 (`#version 300 es` in src/ui/pages/game/vmFrameRenderer.ts), with an R8 index texture plus a palette texture doing the lookup (lines 233-238), and separate RGBA and RGB565 programs.
The VmFrame shape (src/vm86/win32.ts:102-125) is as described: pixels plus palette, optional rgba or rgb565, and a separate cursor bitmap.

setUpscaleMode and setPostProcess exist (vmFrameRenderer.ts:40,42). framePostProcess.ts is documented as a single-pass GLSL ES host. src/graphics/experimental/reshadeLaser.ts exists. The liveModel experiment rejects frames larger than 800x600 (liveModel.ts:97). The ONNX paths are gated to DEV (modelProbe.ts:15).
The docs/RESHADE_ADAPTATION.md:30 quote ('Final frames alone cannot reproduce plugin water, occlusion, or layered high-resolution drawing') and the Toumao DLL strings are accurate.
There is no Ares, Phobos or Syringe support: a word-boundary grep over src and docs gives zero hits.

Campaign support is limited to shell compensation (src/games/ra2/profile.ts campaignMenu; src/vm86/shim/gameProfile.ts). No campaign test exists in tests/real-game (ra2: boot, chooseMap, dropdownRendering, gonghui, saveLoad, shortGame, skirmishSlots, startupPage; yr: boot, saveLoad, spawnerProbe, startupPage). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:63 says YR keeps its previous campaign policy until it is validated separately.
There is a save/load test for both RA2 and YR (tests/real-game/{ra2,yr}/saveLoad.test.ts). The data is serialized into the project's own SGBYSTG1 container, per ARCHITECTURE.md.
There is no reconnect or resume (docs/RA2_NETWORK_RELIABILITY.md:47,88).

src/games/manifest.ts:64-65 and :100-101 hard-code the oldgame.store executable URLs and SHA-256 hashes. src/main.ts:15 calls preloadThirdPartyFiles at load. gameSourcePicker.ts always overlays the fixed executable, with the comment 'shim addresses depend on exact version-sensitive bytes'. downloadCatalog.ts links to uc129.com, jb51.net and archive.org.
The hook pattern is hash-gated. spawnerProbe.ts throws when the executable hash does not match, and runtimeHooks.prepareImage is invoked from src/adapter/vmCore.ts:241.
There are 12 commits on main and the last one is the PR #2 merge (f25986b).
verdict_notes:
Most of the evaluation holds up under re-inspection. The build succeeds (about 8.5 s), all 918 unit tests pass, the renderer is WebGL2 with no Three.js, the hook and file claims are accurate, there is no Ares/Phobos, and campaigns are not regression-tested. What it overstates is how rigid the architecture is for Step 2.

(a) The shim already exposes every DirectDraw surface to the host through inspectSurfaceObjects() and inspectSurface(), so the host is not limited to the final frame.

(b) The host already reads guest memory at fixed YR 1.001 addresses that line up with YRpp: the frame-counter global 0xA8ED84 matches, and the repo's doc says it checked the EventClass/QueueClass layouts against both executables. For YR, then, a game-state and mask bridge can build on a public address map instead of reverse engineering from scratch.

(c) The 1920x1080 limit is only a UI whitelist.

The core conclusion still stands. HD sprites, modern water and effects need a new host-side compositor, the guest still software-renders at 1:1 pixel scale, and RA2 1.006 (as opposed to YR) has no public address map.

Technical reasons I kept the score from going higher:
- Every patch is pinned to a third-party executable hash that is not the retail build.
- The HD bridge exists only as a LaserBlit passthrough.
- Emulation cost at high resolution is unmeasured.

The legal and repo-age points are outside this technical lens. I did not dispute them.

From this lens I raise the score from 4 to 5: it is a strong Step 1 base, and for Step 2 it is a feasible but large YR-first "state bridge plus host compositor" project, with a documented precedent (the Toumao ReShade hooks). I did not run the dev server, real-game tests or nasm. No game assets or EA executables were downloaded.
